newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsubishi Oil, Mobil to share oil distribution.
newsitem.headline: Mitsubishi Oil, Mobil to share oil distribution.

text.p: Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd and Mobil Sekiyu KK plan a sharing arrangement in their oil distribution systems that will save them a combined 1.2 billion yen annually, the companies said on Thursday.
The two companies said they will begin supplying each other with an annual total of 800,000 kilolitres (kl) of oil products sometime during the second-half of fiscal year 1998/99.
Most Japanese firms follow an April/March business year.
The products to be exchanged are gasoline, gas oil, kerosene and fuel oil A, spokesmen for the companies said.
Kyokuto Petroleum Industries Ltd, a member of the Mobil group, will supply Mitsubishi Oil with the products covered by the agreement.
Mobil will receive 400,000 kl of oil products from Tohoku Oil Co Ltd, a member of the Mitsubishi Oil group, and another 400,000 kl from Mitsubishi Oil.
Under Thursday's deal, Mitsubishi Oil and Mobil have also agreed to share Mobil's oil terminal in Fukuoka on the southern island of Kyushu.
Mitsubishi Oil will close its existing oil terminal in Fukuoka following the agreement, which will take effect from April 1998, they said.
The joint terminal will have an annual handling capacity of 250,000 kl for Mitsubishi Oil and 300,000 kl for Mobil.
Japanese oil companies are stepping up their efforts to cooperate in the area of distribution in order to cope with the challenges posed by deregulation.
In April 1996, Japanese oil companies lost their virtually exclusive right to import petroleum products, triggering cut-throat industry competition.
Late last month Mitsubishi Oil said that it and General Sekiyu KK were thinking of supplying each other with oil products. General Sekiyu is owned 49 percent by Exxon Corp .
